back: One-step nucleophilic substitution: Nu attacks from the back as X leaves; rate = k[RX][Nu]; inversion.
Two steps: slow ionisation to a carbocation, then fast attack by Nu; rate = k[RX]; racemisation.
Primary: SN2. Tertiary: SN1. Secondary: both.
Tertiary carbocation stabilised by three alkyl groups (inductive effect); bulky groups block backside attack (steric hindrance).
Highest-energy arrangement with partial bonds; cannot be isolated (unlike an intermediate).

front: SN2 transition state for OH⁻ + RBr
back: [HO···C···Br]⁻: partial C–O and C–Br bonds, three other groups in a plane, overall −1 charge.

front: Using rate data to decide the mechanism
back: Rate depends on [OH⁻] → SN2; independent of [OH⁻] → SN1.
Aqueous OH⁻ favours substitution (alcohol); ethanolic OH⁻, hot, favours elimination (alkene).
SN2: inversion (single enantiomer). SN1: racemic mixture.
